headline: Flames’ Devin Cooley exits game with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Flames goalie Devin Cooley left Tuesday's game with a lower-body injury, and that forward Brennan Othmann also exited with an upper-body injury. Calgary hasn't been healthy in other ways either, sitting at 5-6-0.

Cooley's loss matters most. So far this season he has a .914 save percentage and 2.42 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the quality of shots against him would predict), a big reason the team's goaltending has stayed afloat. CGY as a whole sits at minus 4.7 in that stat, so a netminder beating the model is one thing this team can't easily replace. Last season he put up 17.23 over 31 games, so the early numbers fit a pattern. Othmann is a smaller story. He has no points in five games and his team gets 34 percent of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, 15 points worse than without him, so Calgary's chances don't fall off a cliff in his absence. We have nothing on who absorbs the minutes for either player, so the next few games will show how Calgary shuffles things.
